description:
Attach an organization connector to a website or agent so it can call the connector's tools with the credential Valet holds.

Attaching is a grant, and it is wider than it looks: for a website, every person who can open the page can call every tool the connector exposes. On a private website that is every member of the organization; on a password-protected or shared one it is everyone holding the password or the link. For an agent, the agent can. Valet does not narrow the connector's reach, so attach only what the thing needs, and check a website's access mode before you do.

A website can hold only an organization connector that is an HTTP MCP server, on the sse or streamable-http transport; list_connectors with name marks which ones. A page calls the connector by its own name, which list_connector_tools reports. An app cannot hold a connector yet and the call says so. A connector that belongs to a single agent cannot be attached to anything else. Attaching a connector that is already attached changes nothing and is safe to repeat. Requires connecting a Valet account.

connector.description: The organization connector's name, which is also the name it is called by.

org_name.description: The Valet organization both belong to. Omit to use the organization the account joined first.

name: attach_connector

already_attached.description: True when the connector was already attached before this call, so the call changed nothing. Absent otherwise.

attached.description: True when the holder now holds the connector (attach_connector). Always false from detach_connector.

connector.description: Name of the organization connector, which is also the name the holder calls it by.

kind.description: Kind of the holder named in name: site or agent. The grant means something different for each.

name.description: Name of the website or agent the connector was attached to or detached from.

org.description: Name of the Valet organization the call acted in.

title: Attach a connector
